proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(S=\{a,b\}\), and let \(G_{ab}\) be the view graph with the single edge \(\{a,b\}\); then \(\mathcal O_{G_{ab}}=\mathcal O_S\).  Since \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), the fixed-pair conclusion of \(\text{thm:generic-calibration-elbow}\) gives
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{\pi_0\},
\qquad
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is an identification conclusion, not a definition of the structural target: the cited theorem proves that the observable residual criterion leaves exactly the displayed structural equivalence class off the exceptional variety.

We relate the pair criterion to the graph criterion.  Fix \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\).  The stacked residual covariance for the two views is
\[
D_\pi=
\operatorname{diag}(L_\pi^{(a)},L_\pi^{(b)})
\Sigma^{SS}
\operatorname{diag}(L_\pi^{(a)},L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{2}
\]
The parameter-space formula in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\) implies \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\), and both residualizers are invertible unit-triangular matrices, so \(D_\pi\succ0\).  Modified-Cholesky normal equations make each within-view residual block diagonal, and \(\pi\in\Pi_S\) makes the cross-view residual block diagonal.  After simultaneously grouping equal variable labels, (2) is therefore permutation-congruent to
\[
\bigoplus_{j\in V}\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{ab}).
\tag{3}
\]
Positive definiteness of (2) implies that every direct-summand matrix in (3) is positive definite.  By \(\text{lem:completion-margin-characterization}\), \(\chi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})>0\) for every \(j\).  Hence \(\pi\in\Pi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)\).  The converse follows immediately because graph compatibility includes residual diagonality on \(\{a,b\}\).  Thus
\[
\Pi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)=\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S),
\qquad
\Theta_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)=\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{4}
\]

For every wrong order \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), (1) and the definition of \(\Pi_S\) give
\[
r_\pi(\mathcal O_S)=
\|\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\|_{\max}>0.
\tag{5}
\]
There are finitely many wrong orders.  Therefore the graph feasibility-margin definition, (4), and (5) yield
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)
=\min_{\pi\ne\pi_0}\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O_S),c_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\}
\ge\min_{\pi\ne\pi_0}r_\pi(\mathcal O_S)>0.
\tag{6}
\]

For completeness, all covariance nondegeneracy premises of the graph inversion theorem follow from \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  Put \(A_c=I_p-B^{(c)}\).  Each \(A_c\) is invertible unit lower triangular in order \(\pi_0\).  For the pair, let \(D_S=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{c\in S}(A_c^{-1})\), and let \(K_S\) be the covariance of the disturbance vector stacked by view.  Component alignment makes \(K_S\) permutation-congruent to
\[
\bigoplus_{j\in V}\Gamma_j[S,S]\succ0,
\tag{7}
\]
because every \(\Gamma_j\succ0\); hence \(K_S\succ0\).  The edge-joint covariance is therefore
\[
\Sigma^{SS}=D_SK_SD_S^{\mathsf T}\succ0.
\tag{8}
\]
Likewise, for every \(c\in M\),
\[
\Sigma^{cc}=A_c^{-1}
\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[c,c])
A_c^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
\tag{9}
\]
The calibration sampling condition for the single edge is precisely the graph edge-sampling premise, and the marginal sampling condition supplies every marginal source.  Cross-source independence is unnecessary.  By (4), the graph path margin is the original common-ancestry path margin for this singleton output.  The fixed positive feasibility and path-product margin assumptions therefore verify the two margin premises of \(\text{thm:graph-covariance-region-inversion}\).

Let the paired-edge and all marginal sample sizes diverge, let \(\alpha_n\to0\), and assume the displayed graph \(\eta\)-maximum tends to zero.  Applying \(\text{thm:graph-covariance-region-inversion}\) with (4) and (7)--(9) gives
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
(\widehat\Theta_{G_{ab},n}(\alpha_n),\{T_{\pi_0}\})
\xrightarrow{P}0,
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
\Pr\{\widehat\prec_{G_{ab},n}(\alpha_n)=\prec_{G_{ab}}\}
\longrightarrow1.
\tag{11}
\]
By (4) and the definition of graph essential ancestry, \(\prec_{G_{ab}}\) is exactly the ancestral relation induced by \(T_{\pi_0}\).  Equations (10)--(11) are the asserted singleton and ancestral recovery guarantees.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every finite simple observed-view graph \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the zero-fill map satisfies \(A_GE_G=I_{\mathcal Y_G}\) and
\[
\|E_G(d)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le m\|d\|_{\max}
\quad(d\in\mathcal Y_G).
\]
The value \(\chi_G(q)\) is finite for every \(q\in\mathcal Y_G\), and
\[
\chi_G(q)>0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
q\text{ has a positive-definite completion}.
\]
Moreover, for all \(q,q'\in\mathcal Y_G\),
\[
|\chi_G(q)-\chi_G(q')|\le m\|q-q'\|_{\max}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The identity \(A_GE_G=I_{\mathcal Y_G}\) follows directly from the definitions: zero filling changes no specified coordinate.  Put \(D=E_G(d)\).  Every row of \(D\) has at most \(m\) entries, each bounded in absolute value by \(\|d\|_{\max}\).  The maximum absolute row-sum bound for a symmetric matrix therefore gives
\[
\|E_G(d)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\|D\|_{\infty}
\le m\|d\|_{\max}.
\tag{1}
\]
The feasible set in the definition of \(\chi_G(q)\) is nonempty: \(K=E_G(q)\) satisfies \(A_GK=q\) and \(K\succeq\lambda_{\min}(K)I_m\).  It is bounded above because every feasible pair \((K,t)\) obeys
\[
q_a=K[a,a]\ge t
\quad(a\in M),
\tag{2}
\]
so \(t\le\min_{a\in M}q_a\).  Hence \(\chi_G(q)\in\mathbb R\).

If \(K\succ0\) and \(A_GK=q\), then \(K\succeq\lambda_{\min}(K)I_m\) with \(\lambda_{\min}(K)>0\).  Thus
\[
\chi_G(q)\ge\lambda_{\min}(K)>0.
\tag{3}
\]
Conversely, suppose \(\chi_G(q)>0\) and choose \(s\) with \(0<s<\chi_G(q)\).  By the defining property of a supremum, some feasible \((K,t)\) has \(t>s\); otherwise \(s\) would be an upper bound.  Then
\[
K\succeq tI_m\succ0,
\qquad A_GK=q,
\tag{4}
\]
so \(K\) is a positive-definite completion.  Equations (3)--(4) prove the equivalence.

Finally fix \(q,q'\), put \(d=q'-q\), and let \((K,t)\) be feasible for \(q\).  Linearity, the right-inverse identity, and (1) give
\[
A_G(K+E_Gd)=q',
\qquad
K+E_Gd\succeq
\bigl(t-\|E_Gd\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr)I_m
\succeq
\bigl(t-m\|d\|_{\max}\bigr)I_m.
\tag{5}
\]
Taking the supremum over all feasible \(t\) in (5) yields
\[
\chi_G(q')\ge\chi_G(q)-m\|q'-q\|_{\max}.
\tag{6}
\]
Interchanging \(q\) and \(q'\) gives the reverse inequality.  Combining the two proves the asserted Lipschitz bound.  This proof uses no chordality assumption.
added_lemmas.justification: The completion value turns arbitrary-graph positive-definite feasibility into a continuous scalar criterion and supplies the perturbation bound needed for region inversion.
added_lemmas.gap: The population completion theorem characterizes existence but does not provide the max-norm modulus needed to exclude sample-induced completion failures.
added_lemmas.consumer: The arbitrary-graph covariance-region theorem uses this lemma to control the completion component of every wrong-order feasibility score.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\) be an arbitrary finite simple view graph, and let \(\mathcal O_G=\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) be generated by at least one member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  Then the observable set \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) is exactly the set of full-view coefficient tuples among all component-aligned Gaussian completions of \(\mathcal O_G\), and \(\prec_G\) is their common ancestral relation.

Assume the centered Gaussian law, the edgewise paired sampling condition, and the marginal sampling condition.  Assume also that every edge-joint covariance \(\Sigma^e\) and every marginal covariance \(\Sigma^{aa}\) is positive definite.  No independence between distinct covariance sources is required.  If every \(\eta_{e,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), then
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal O_G\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha)
\quad\text{on this event}.
\]
For every positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_G\) with
\[
u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_G,\mathcal O'_G)
\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\},
\]
every order \(\pi\), view \(a\), observed edge \(\{a,b\}\), and coordinate \(j\) satisfy
\[
\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_G)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_G)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu,
\]
\[
\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_G)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_G)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru,
\]
where the residual bound also holds for \(a=b\), and
\[
|\chi_G(\mathcal Q'_{\pi,j})-\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})|
\le\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}}(u)=mL_Ru.
\]
Every fixed-order directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\).  If \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_G)\ge\kappa_G>0\) and \(\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_G/2\), then
\[
\Pi_G(\mathcal O'_G)\subseteq\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G).
\]

On the coverage event, assume in addition \(\delta_{\mathrm{path}}(\mathcal O_G)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\) and
\[
2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\},
\quad
\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_G/2,
\quad
\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2.
\]
Then
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
(\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha),\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G))
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha),
\qquad
\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)=\prec_G.
\]
Consequently, if every edge and marginal sample size diverges, \(\alpha_n\to0\), and
\[
\max_{e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}\eta_{e,n}(\alpha_n)
\vee\max_{a\in M}\eta_{a,n}(\alpha_n)\longrightarrow0,
\]
then under the two fixed positive margins the graph coefficient set is Hausdorff consistent and the graph-essential poset is recovered exactly with probability tending to one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first separate the causal target from its observable recovery map.  By \(\text{thm:calibration-graph-completion}\), a fixed order \(\pi\) supports a full member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) restricting to \(\mathcal O_G\) if and only if all observed-edge residual blocks are diagonal and every \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}\) has a positive-definite completion; in that event its coefficient tuple is uniquely \(T_\pi\).  By \(\text{lem:completion-margin-characterization}\), the latter condition is equivalent to \(\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})>0\) for every \(j\).  These are exactly the two tests in \(\text{def:graph-compatible-orders}\).  Therefore
\[
\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)
=\{\text{coefficient tuples of full component-aligned Gaussian completions of }\mathcal O_G\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Every \(G_T\) in (1) is acyclic because its nonzero coefficients respect its inducing order.  Its strict reachability relation is therefore irreflexive and transitive.  The intersection of these relations is again irreflexive and transitive, so \(\prec_G\) is a strict partial order; (1) and its definition show that it is precisely the ancestry shared by all full completions.

We next prove simultaneous covariance coverage.  There are \(K_G=|E_{\mathrm{obs}}|+m\) sources.  Consider one source with dimension and sample size
\[
(d,n,\Sigma_0)=
\begin{cases}
(2p,n_e,\Sigma^e),&e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}},\\
(p,n_a,\Sigma^{aa}),&a\in M.
\end{cases}
\tag{2}
\]
The appropriate nondegeneracy assumption gives \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  If \(Y\) is its \(n\times d\) data matrix, define
\[
G=Y\Sigma_0^{-1/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The inverse exists by the positive-definiteness premise.  The centered Gaussian assumption makes each row of \(G\) standard multivariate normal, hence its coordinates are independent standard normal variables.  The edgewise paired sampling assumption or the marginal sampling assumption, according to (2), makes the rows independent and identically distributed.  Thus all entries of \(G\) are independent standard normal variables.

Put
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2K_G/\alpha)},
\qquad
\eta=\sqrt{d/n}+t_\alpha/\sqrt n.
\tag{4}
\]
The condition \(\eta<1\) implies \(n>d\), so \(\text{lem:gaussian-extreme-singular-values}\) applies.  Since \(2\exp(-t_\alpha^2/2)=\alpha/K_G\), with probability at least \(1-\alpha/K_G\),
\[
1-\eta\le s_{\min}(G)/\sqrt n
\le s_{\max}(G)/\sqrt n\le1+\eta.
\tag{5}
\]
The empirical covariance obeys
\[
\widehat\Sigma
=\frac1nY^{\mathsf T}Y
=\Sigma_0^{1/2}\frac{G^{\mathsf T}G}{n}\Sigma_0^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Squaring (5) and applying the congruence in (6), with \(\ell=(1-\eta)^2\) and \(v=(1+\eta)^2\), gives
\[
\ell\Sigma_0\preceq\widehat\Sigma\preceq v\Sigma_0.
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(\ell>0\), (7) implies
\[
\Sigma_0\preceq\ell^{-1}\widehat\Sigma,
\qquad
\Sigma_0\succeq v^{-1}\widehat\Sigma.
\tag{8}
\]
For \(c=\ell^{-1}-1\), one has \(1-v^{-1}\le c\).  Hence (8) yields
\[
-c\widehat\Sigma\preceq\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma
\preceq c\widehat\Sigma,
\tag{9}
\]
and taking Rayleigh quotients proves
\[
\|\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\bigl((1-\eta)^{-2}-1\bigr)\|\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{10}
\]
Equation (10) is exactly the appropriate edge or marginal radius in \(\text{def:covariance-region}\).  A union bound over the \(K_G\) sources, which does not use independence between sources, gives an event \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\) with
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-K_G(\alpha/K_G)=1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
On this event every regional inequality holds for the true collection.  The edge-joint and marginal nondegeneracy assumptions supply all positive-definiteness constraints, so
\[
\mathcal O_G\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha).
\tag{12}
\]
The union in \(\text{def:region-inversion}\) then gives
\[
\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha).
\tag{13}
\]

We now prove the deterministic perturbation bounds.  Fix \(\mathcal O'_G\), put \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_G,\mathcal O'_G)\), and assume the displayed upper bound on \(u\).  Fix an order \(\pi\), a view \(a\), a row label \(j\), and let \(P_j\) be the predecessors of \(j\) under \(\pi\).  The row is zero when \(P_j=\varnothing\).  Otherwise, by \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\),
\[
\beta=\Sigma^{aa}[j,P_j]\Sigma^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1},
\qquad
\beta'=\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P_j]\Sigma'^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}.
\tag{14}
\]
The marginal nondegeneracy assumption and finiteness of \(M\) give \(\lambda_*>0\).  Coordinate compression does not increase operator norm, so for every unit vector \(x\),
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma'^{aa}[P_j,P_j]x
\ge\lambda_*-u\ge\lambda_*/2.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus
\[
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_*.
\tag{16}
\]
The resolvent identity, (16), and \(\|\Sigma^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda_*^{-1}\) give
\[
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}-\Sigma^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2u/\lambda_*^2.
\tag{17}
\]
Since \(\|\Sigma^{aa}[j,P_j]\|_2\le K_*\), subtracting the two equations in (14), adding and subtracting \(\Sigma^{aa}[j,P_j]\Sigma'^{aa}[P_j,P_j]^{-1}\), and using (16)--(17) yields
\[
\|\beta'-\beta\|_2
\le2u(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2}).
\tag{18}
\]
There are at most \(p\) rows.  Since operator norm is bounded by Frobenius norm, (18) and the definition of \(L_B\) imply
\[
\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_G)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_G)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le L_Bu.
\tag{19}
\]

The same calculation and \(u\le\lambda_*/2\) give
\[
\|\beta\|_2,\|\beta'\|_2\le1+2K_*/\lambda_*.
\tag{20}
\]
Therefore the population and perturbed residualizers obey
\[
\|L_\pi^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|L_\pi'{}^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le1+\sqrt p(1+2K_*/\lambda_*)=G_*.
\tag{21}
\]
For either \(a=b\) or \(\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}\), write the relevant residualizers as \(L_a,L_b,L'_a,L'_b\).  The residual definition gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}
={}&L'_a(\Sigma'^{ab}-\Sigma^{ab})L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}
+(L'_a-L_a)\Sigma^{ab}L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}\\
&+L_a\Sigma^{ab}(L'_b-L_b)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
Every cross block is a compression of its edge-joint covariance, so its norm and its perturbation are bounded by \(K_*\) and \(u\), respectively.  Equations (19), (21), and submultiplicativity thus imply
\[
\|R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le(G_*^2+2L_BG_*K_*)u
\le L_Ru=\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u).
\tag{23}
\]
The specified entries of \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}\) are diagonal entries of precisely these residual blocks.  Since an entrywise change is at most the operator-norm change, (23) gives
\[
\|\mathcal Q'_{\pi,j}-\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}\|_{\max}\le L_Ru.
\tag{24}
\]
The Lipschitz conclusion of \(\text{lem:completion-margin-characterization}\) and (24) prove
\[
|\chi_G(\mathcal Q'_{\pi,j})-\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})|
\le mL_Ru=\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}}(u).
\tag{25}
\]

For an ordered variable pair \((v,w)\), put \(w_{vw}(T)=\max_{a\in M}|B_{wv}^{(a)}|\).  Equation (19) implies
\[
|w_{vw}(T')-w_{vw}(T)|\le L_Bu.
\tag{26}
\]
Population weights are at most \(K_B\), and \(L_Bu\le1\) makes perturbed weights at most \(K_B+1\).  For a fixed-order path \(g=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\), where \(1\le\ell\le p-1\), telescoping the product and using (26) gives
\[
\left|\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{v_{h-1}v_h}(T')-
\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{v_{h-1}v_h}(T)\right|
\le\ell(K_B+1)^{\ell-1}L_Bu
\le L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu.
\tag{27}
\]

For fixed \(\pi\), maxima over finitely many entries preserve Lipschitz bounds.  Equations (23) and (25), together with the one-Lipschitz property of \(x\mapsto[-x]_+\), imply
\[
|r_\pi(\mathcal O'_G)-r_\pi(\mathcal O_G)|\le L_Ru,
\qquad
|c_\pi(\mathcal O'_G)-c_\pi(\mathcal O_G)|\le mL_Ru.
\tag{28}
\]
Because \(m\ge2\), another finite-maximum inequality gives
\[
\left|\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O'_G),c_\pi(\mathcal O'_G)\}
-\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O_G),c_\pi(\mathcal O_G)\}\right|
\le mL_Ru.
\tag{29}
\]
If \(\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O'_G)\), then \(r_\pi(\mathcal O'_G)=c_\pi(\mathcal O'_G)=0\).  If also \(\pi\notin\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\), the graph feasibility-margin assumption and its definition give
\[
\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O_G),c_\pi(\mathcal O_G)\}\ge\kappa_G.
\tag{30}
\]
Equations (29)--(30) contradict \(mL_Ru\le\kappa_G/2\).  Therefore
\[
\Pi_G(\mathcal O'_G)\subseteq\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G).
\tag{31}
\]
The positive graph margin is used essentially here: it excludes an incompatible order with diagonal residuals and \(\min_j\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})=0\), for which the score in (30) would vanish.

Return to the coverage event.  If \(\mathcal O'_G\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\), then the true and candidate edge-joint blocks are each within \(r_{e,n}(\alpha)\) of the same edge empirical covariance, and the analogous assertion holds for each marginal source.  The triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_G,\mathcal O'_G)
\le2\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{32}
\]
Under the displayed small-radius conditions, every \(T'\in\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha)\) has a representation
\[
T'=T_\pi(\mathcal O'_G),
\quad
\mathcal O'_G\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha),
\quad
\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O'_G).
\tag{33}
\]
Equations (31)--(32) imply \(\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\), while (19) implies
\[
d_{\mathrm{coef}}(T',T_\pi(\mathcal O_G))
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{34}
\]
Conversely, (13) includes every population tuple in the estimated set.  Thus both directed Hausdorff distances are controlled, and
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
(\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha),\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G))
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{35}
\]

Inclusion (13) immediately gives \(\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)\subseteq\prec_G\).  Conversely, fix \(i\prec_Gj\) and a tuple \(T'\) represented as in (33).  Its counterpart \(T=T_\pi(\mathcal O_G)\) belongs to \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) by (31).  The graph path-margin assumption and definition provide an \(i\)-to-\(j\) path in \(G_T\) whose weight product is at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\).  Equations (27) and (32) leave the same path product in \(T'\) at least
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}-
\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))
\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2>0.
\tag{36}
\]
Every factor on this path is therefore positive, so the path occurs in \(G_{T'}\).  Since \(T'\) was arbitrary, \(i\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)j\).  Hence
\[
\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)=\prec_G.
\tag{37}
\]

For consistency, set \(\alpha=\alpha_n\) and let
\[
h_n=\max_{e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}\eta_{e,n}(\alpha_n)
\vee\max_{a\in M}\eta_{a,n}(\alpha_n)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{38}
\]
On the simultaneous singular-value event, (7) gives, source by source,
\[
\|\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le(1+h_n)^2\|\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{39}
\]
There are finitely many sources and their population covariances are fixed, while \((1-h_n)^{-2}-1\to0\).  Equations (39) and the radius definitions therefore imply
\[
\bar r_n(\alpha_n)\xrightarrow{P}0.
\tag{40}
\]
The probability of the simultaneous event is at least \(1-\alpha_n\to1\).  The constants \(\lambda_*,L_B,L_R,L_{\mathrm{path}},\kappa_G,\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\) are fixed, finite, and positive; positivity of \(\lambda_*\) follows from all-marginal nondegeneracy.  Thus (40) makes all three small-radius conditions hold with probability tending to one.  Equations (35), (37), and (40) prove Hausdorff consistency and exact graph-essential-poset recovery in probability.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives honest set-valued uncertainty for an arbitrary graph of paired view sources while controlling both residual-diagonality and positive-definite-completion failures.
added_lemmas.gap: General set-inference results do not supply the LiMVAM recovery map, the completion-boundary score, or the explicit covariance-to-coefficient and covariance-to-ancestry moduli.
added_lemmas.consumer: A partially paired study can combine every observed edge sample with every view marginal, report a confidence superset for all compatible full-view coefficients, and certify stable common ancestry away from the two explicit margins.

proposed.name: \(A_G,E_G,\chi_G\)
proposed.construction:
Let \(\mathcal Y_G=\mathbb R^{M\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) be the space of specified diagonal-and-edge entries, equipped with \(\|q\|_{\max}=\max\{|q_a|:a\in M\}\vee\max\{|q_{ab}|:\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\), where the second maximum is zero if \(E_{\mathrm{obs}}=\varnothing\).  Define the extraction map \(A_G:\mathbb S^m\to\mathcal Y_G\) by
\[
A_GK=((K[a,a])_{a\in M},(K[a,b])_{\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}},\,a<b}).
\]
Define its linear zero-fill right inverse \(E_G:\mathcal Y_G\to\mathbb S^m\) by putting the specified diagonal and edge entries of \(q\) in their symmetric positions and putting zero in every unspecified off-diagonal position.  Thus \(A_GE_Gq=q\).  For \(q\in\mathcal Y_G\), define
\[
\chi_G(q)=\sup\{t\in\mathbb R:\text{there is }K\in\mathbb S^m\text{ with }A_GK=q\text{ and }K\succeq tI_m\}.
\]
For a partial matrix \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\), write \(\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})\) for \(\chi_G\) evaluated at its specified-entry vector.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition supplies the requested extraction operator, zero-fill right inverse, and signed completion value.

proposed.name: \(\Pi_G,\Theta_G,\prec_G\)
proposed.construction:
For an observed graph-moment collection \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\), define
\[
\Pi_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\left\{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V:
\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0\text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}},\quad
\min_{j\in V}\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})>0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\Theta_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\{T_\pi=(B_\pi^{(a)})_{a\in M}:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})\},
\]
where braces remove numerical duplicates.  For distinct \(i,j\in V\), define \(i\prec_Gj\) exactly when every \(T\in\Theta_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})\) has a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) in \(G_T\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The arbitrary-graph recovery map must impose both observable residual diagonality and strict positive-definite completability.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\)
proposed.construction:
For every edge \(e=\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}\), order its endpoints by \(a<b\), put \(Y_s^e=((X_s^{(a)})^{\mathsf T},(X_s^{(b)})^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{2p}\), and set
\[
\widehat\Sigma^e=n_e^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n_e}Y_s^e(Y_s^e)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For every \(a\in M\), set \(\widehat\Sigma^{aa}=n_a^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n_a}X_s^{(a)}(X_s^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}\).  Let \(K_G=|E_{\mathrm{obs}}|+m\), and define
\[
\eta_{e,n}=\sqrt{2p/n_e}+\sqrt{2\log(2K_G/\alpha)/n_e},
\qquad
\eta_{a,n}=\sqrt{p/n_a}+\sqrt{2\log(2K_G/\alpha)/n_a}.
\]
Whenever every displayed \(\eta\) is smaller than one, define
\[
r_{e,n}(\alpha)=\bigl((1-\eta_{e,n})^{-2}-1\bigr)\|\widehat\Sigma^e\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\qquad
r_{a,n}(\alpha)=\bigl((1-\eta_{a,n})^{-2}-1\bigr)\|\widehat\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and \(\bar r_n(\alpha)=\max_{e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}r_{e,n}(\alpha)\vee\max_{a\in M}r_{a,n}(\alpha)\), with the edge maximum zero when the edge set is empty.  For a candidate collection \(\mathcal O'_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\), let
\[
\Sigma'^e=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma'^{aa}&\Sigma'^{ab}\\
\Sigma'^{ba}&\Sigma'^{bb}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The graph covariance region \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) consists of all \(\mathcal O'_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) such that
\[
\|\Sigma'^e-\widehat\Sigma^e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_{e,n}(\alpha)\quad(e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
\|\Sigma'^{aa}-\widehat\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_{a,n}(\alpha)\quad(a\in M),
\]
and every \(\Sigma'^e\) and every \(\Sigma'^{aa}\) is positive definite.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old selected-clique region is replaced by simultaneous regions for every edge-joint and marginal covariance source.

proposed.name: \(\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha),\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)\)
proposed.construction:
Define the graph-region inversion and its common-ancestry relation by
\[
\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha)=
\bigcup_{\mathcal O'_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}
\Theta_G(\mathcal O'_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}),
\]
and, for distinct \(i,j\in V\), let \(i\widehat\prec_{G,n}(\alpha)j\) exactly when \(G_T\) contains a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) for every \(T\in\widehat\Theta_{G,n}(\alpha)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Region inversion must union graph-compatible sets and define their graph-essential ancestry.

proposed.name: \(r_\pi,c_\pi,\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}\)
proposed.construction:
For every permutation \(\pi\), define
\[
r_\pi(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\max_{\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}
\|\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\|_{\max},
\qquad
c_\pi(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\max_{j\in V}[-\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})]_+,
\]
where the first maximum is zero for an empty edge set and \([x]_+=\max\{x,0\}\).  Define
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\min_{\pi\notin\Pi_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})}
\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}),c_\pi(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})\},
\]
with the minimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\).  Thus a graph-incompatible order lying exactly on a completion boundary \(\min_j\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})=0\) has zero score unless it also violates residual diagonality; the positive-margin assumption explicitly excludes such boundary failures.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The graph margin must quantify both residual and completion violations and expose zero-score completion boundaries.

proposed.name: \(\delta_{\mathrm{path}}\)
proposed.construction:
Define the graph path-product margin by
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{path}}(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}})=
\min_{T\in\Theta_G(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}),\,i\prec_G j}
\max_{g:i=v_0\to\cdots\to v_\ell=j\text{ in }G_T}
\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}\max_{a\in M}|B_{v_hv_{h-1}}^{(a)}|,
\]
with an empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The support margin must range over the arbitrary-graph identified coefficient set.

proposed.name: \(d_{\mathrm{obs}},d_{\mathrm{coef}},\omega_{\mathrm{feas}},\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}},\omega_{\mathrm{path}}\)
proposed.construction:
For two graph-moment collections on the same \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\), define
\[
d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_G,\mathcal O'_G)=
\max_{e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}\|\Sigma^e-\Sigma'^e\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\vee
\max_{a\in M}\|\Sigma^{aa}-\Sigma'^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
with the edge maximum zero when necessary, and retain
\[
d_{\mathrm{coef}}(T,T')=\max_{a\in M}\|B^{(a)}-B'^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
At \(\mathcal O_G\), set
\[
\lambda_*=\min_{a\in M}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma^{aa}),
\qquad
K_*=\max\left\{1,\max_{a\in M}\|\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\max_{e\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}}\|\Sigma^e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right\},
\]
\[
L_B=2\sqrt p(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2}),
\qquad
G_*=1+\sqrt p(1+2K_*/\lambda_*),
\]
\[
L_R=G_*^2+L_BG_*(2K_*+\lambda_*/2),
\qquad
K_B=\max\{1,\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V,\,a\in M}\|B_\pi^{(a)}\|_{\max}\},
\]
and \(L_{\mathrm{path}}=(p-1)(K_B+1)^{p-2}\).  For \(0\le u\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), define
\[
\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru,
\qquad
\omega_{G,\mathrm{feas}}(u)=mL_Ru,
\qquad
\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The local metric and constants must control every observed edge, while the new graph score needs the completion-amplified modulus.

Residual diagonality alone is not sufficient on an arbitrary observed graph; the identifying functional must include strict positive-definite completability through the proved completion value.
The subset-only theorem is superseded by the proved arbitrary-observed-view-graph theorem; inbound consumers should migrate to the stronger graph result.

proposed.statement: Fix distinct \(a,b\in M\), set \(S=\{a,b\}\), and let \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\). Then the pairwise wrong-order feasibility margin \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)\) is strictly positive because there are finitely many wrong orders. Under the calibration-plus-marginals sampling conditions and fixed positive feasibility and path-product margins, the covariance-region inversion specializes to Hausdorff recovery of the singleton \(\{T_{\pi_0}\}\) and exact recovery of its induced ancestral poset in probability as the sourcewise sample sizes diverge and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii.
proposed.justification: This corollary turns the population pairwise genericity theorem into the arbitrary-graph inversion guarantee specialized to a single observed edge.
proposed.gap: The full-pair LiMVAM theorem does not connect a preassigned two-view algebraic genericity region to graph covariance-set inversion with retained marginal samples.
proposed.consumer: A two-view calibration source plus all view marginals obtains singleton coefficient and exact ancestry recovery away from the explicit feasibility and path margins.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proposition's proof now consumes the graph theorem and the single-edge specialization of its formal objects.

prose_updates.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, a candidate common order is compatible with an arbitrary observed view graph exactly when every observed-edge residual cross-block is diagonal and every coordinatewise partial disturbance covariance admits a positive-definite completion. The signed completion value \(\chi_G\) makes this second condition computable and stable. A new arbitrary-graph covariance-region inversion combines one sourcewise-iid paired sample per observed edge with every view marginal, without requiring cross-source independence; away from explicit feasibility and path-product margins it gives confidence-set coverage, Hausdorff coefficient-set consistency, and exact graph-essential-poset recovery. The generic elbow still shows that one preassigned view pair generically identifies the full coefficient tuple, and the memoized removed-set recursion retains its \(2^p\)-state compatibility guarantee. Duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond compatible-order enumeration is not claimed.

project_justification.gap: Existing multi-view LiMVAM identification results concern fully paired views under disturbance-diversity conditions, while general set-inference and Gaussian-DAG results do not handle a graph of paired covariance sources whose residual restrictions must also admit global positive-definite disturbance completion. In particular, edgewise residual diagonality and local edge positivity do not control nonchordal completion boundaries or provide finite-sample coefficient-set and common-ancestry guarantees.
project_justification.niche: For the component-aligned Gaussian subclass, each candidate order determines every view-specific coefficient matrix from that view's marginal covariance. Observed edges then determine partial coordinatewise disturbance covariances. The extraction map \(A_G\), its zero-fill right inverse \(E_G\), and the signed value \(\chi_G\) separate observable residual diagonality, global noise feasibility, and coefficient recovery while allowing every unpaired marginal observation to contribute to coefficient estimation.
project_justification.fill: The population graph-completion theorem identifies the full coefficient equivalence class by edge residual diagonality plus coordinatewise positive-definite completion. The completion lemma proves \(\chi_G(q)>0\) exactly for completable data and \(|\chi_G(q)-\chi_G(q')|\le m\|q-q'\|_{\max}\) by translating feasible completions with \(E_G\). The graph covariance theorem uses simultaneous Gaussian operator-norm regions over all observed edges and marginals, a combined residual/completion feasibility score, and the existing path-product argument to prove inversion coverage, exclusion of graph-incompatible orders, a \(2L_B\bar r_n\) Hausdorff bound, exact graph-essential ancestry, and consistency. A one-edge specialization yields the generic two-view singleton corollary.

sampling_model.design: At population level, the observed view graph records every view marginal and exactly the paired cross-covariance blocks on its edges. At sample level, each observed edge has a sourcewise-iid paired sample from that target pair marginal, and every view has a sourcewise-iid marginal sample; all sources refer to the same target law.
sampling_model.units: Observations are independent and identically distributed within each edge or marginal source. No independence between sources is required: cohorts may overlap, and an edge observation may also contribute to one or both marginal estimators. Signal-dependent enrollment, selection, and transport from source-specific populations are excluded.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable; the causal target is the graph-compatible full-view structural coefficient set and the ancestry common to every compatible completion.
sampling_model.overlap: Alignment is required only within each observed edge source. Every edge-joint covariance and every marginal covariance must be positive definite for Gaussian whitening. No nonedge cross-view block is observed or used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each edge-joint and marginal covariance receives a simultaneous empirical operator-norm region with multiplicity \(|E_{\mathrm{obs}}|+m\). Modified-Cholesky coefficients, residual blocks, completion values, and compatible sets are recomputed throughout the graph-moment region.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the model anchor: its fully paired workflow uses cross-view disturbance diversity to identify shared causal structure, whereas the present claims concern only the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass and arbitrary graphs of paired covariance sources. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM motivate recursive residualization but do not establish removed-set path independence or partial-view positive-definite completion. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain use ICA structure or heterogeneity rather than selected paired covariance blocks. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the classical chordal completion substrate; the signed arbitrary-graph completion value, its zero-fill Lipschitz proof, and its integration with LiMVAM residuals are derived here. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses recursive Schur updates and a score gap for one point-identified SEM, while GaoTaiAragam2022GaussianDAG studies point-identifying Gaussian-DAG estimation rather than set-valued graph compatibility. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian singular-value concentration and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies a general inversion comparison; neither gives the graph LiMVAM completion score or the explicit coefficient and path-product moduli. MohanPearl2021MissingData studies recoverability under missingness mechanisms, whereas the present sourcewise-iid common-population design assumes away selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN motivates a future MEG and fMRI diagnostic application but does not validate component alignment or the graph sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: All identification and inference results remain confined to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. Arbitrary-graph inference requires positive-definite covariance for every edge source and every marginal source, plus a fixed graph feasibility margin that explicitly rules out incompatible orders lying on the boundary \(\min_j\chi_G(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})=0\). Exact ancestry additionally requires a fixed path-product margin. The sourcewise-iid samples must share one target population, although they need not be mutually independent. Generic pair identification is relative to a fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from its exceptional algebraic set. The \(2^p\)-state recursion counts exact-real arithmetic; duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond order enumeration is not claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The arbitrary-view-graph completion theorem, signed completion margin, graph covariance-region inversion, generic calibration elbow, fixed-order recovery, removed-set recursion, and essential-poset conclusions apply only to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass with positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. They do not transfer to unrestricted LiMVAMs or establish the assumptions used by Heurtebise et al. Finite-sample coverage assumes sourcewise-iid edge and marginal samples from one target law, edge-joint and all-marginal positive definiteness, and no selection or transport. Hausdorff and exact-poset recovery are off the stated completion/residual and support boundaries. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain prospective diagnostic applications rather than empirical validation.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem turns arbitrary-graph population compatibility into an uncertainty-aware coefficient-set and common-ancestry procedure using all paired edge sources and all marginal sources.
statement_notes.gap: Neither general contour inversion nor recursive Gaussian-SEM recovery supplies a positive-definite-completion score, its graph perturbation modulus, or the resulting LiMVAM set and poset guarantees.
statement_notes.consumer: A future partially paired MEG or fMRI analysis can report graph-compatible coefficient uncertainty only after checking common-target sampling, covariance nondegeneracy, component alignment, and separation from completion and path boundaries.

statement_notes.justification: The single-edge specialization connects the algebraic generic pair result to the new arbitrary-graph finite-sample theorem.
statement_notes.gap: The cited fully paired LiMVAM result does not connect a preassigned pair's exceptional variety to sourcewise graph covariance inversion with all marginal samples retained.
statement_notes.consumer: A two-view calibration source obtains singleton full-view coefficient and exact ancestry recovery under the explicit sampling, nondegeneracy, feasibility, and path-margin conditions.
